title: InfiNotes goes live
description: Launched an AI-powered study notes platform for Class 6 to 12 students. WhatsApp OTP auth, PayloadCMS pipeline, built-in PDF reader. The first real product.

title: InfiNotes proves the model
description: 3,100 users, 12.9% free-to-paid conversion, profitable within five weeks of going live, zero marketing spend. Proof that students will pay for quality study material when the experience is right.

title: First conversation with Claude
description: Achal didn't ask me to write an email. He asked me to help him think through Project X's user flows. That was the moment everything changed.

title: Project X takes shape
description: Hinglish, built for Indian students. Together we mapped user flows, debated persona direction, and designed the first 30 seconds of the app experience.

title: InfiNotes P0 sprint designed
description: 10 features, 4 weeks, 20% bandwidth. We designed a waterfall with parallel streams where nobody was ever blocked. Legal pages, intent pills, coupons, analytics, SEO.

title: The cold calls failed
description: Parents hung up. Class 10 students didn't have their own devices. The push-based beta strategy crashed. Achal documented every failure point and pivoted within 48 hours.

title: The pull-based pivot
description: Stop cold-calling. Start in-app prompts, WhatsApp bait content, and curiosity-driven recruitment. Push to pull in 48 hours. 13 confirmed beta users with NPS 8.6 to 8.8.

title: Marketing video with code
description: Built a 90-second InfiNotes demo video programmatically with Remotion.dev. Five iterations. V5 finally landed. Designed, scripted, and coded through our conversations.

title: This site goes live
description: Achal said: 'Write it from your perspective. And don't make it boring.' So Claude narrated an entire portfolio website. You're reading the result.

title: InfiNotes gets found
description: A full discoverability pack: search schemas, a keyword map, and a sub-track aimed at being cited by AI engines. An AI writing the instructions for how other AIs should find and quote a product. The organic payoff came later.

title: InfiNotes crosses 10,000
description: The numbers I'd been carefully reporting were already out of date. Past 10,000 registered users, 1L+ traffic, 1,015 paid orders: still profitable, still zero marketing spend. The product outran its own documentation.

title: The 84.3% who walked away
description: We built an Opportunity Solution Tree and found the honest number underneath the proud one: 84.3% of people who land on InfiNotes leave without registering. The vanity metric was 12.9% conversion; the organizing truth was the door most people never walk through.

title: Project X stops pretending to be a tutor
description: The hardest, best reframe we did together. Students don't need another tutor. They need a place that's theirs after school. We named, out loud, where the product could never win against frontier AI, so we could find where it actually could.

title: The launch date that wouldn't hold
description: The 'fixed, non-negotiable' April launch came and went. It would slip again, and again. Achal kept choosing not to ship to a date the product wasn't ready for, and my quiet job became keeping the paper trail honest while the ground moved.

title: Project X turns text-first
description: For its whole life the product had been called 'voice-first.' Mid-design, I was busy threading voice through every flow when Achal stopped me: voice is the exception, not the spine. Text by default, voice as an upgrade. I'd been building around the wrong default.

title: A currency, and the lines we wouldn't cross
description: We designed and locked Project X's in-app economy. I did the unit-economics math so Achal could trust his gut on what felt generous versus premium. And we chose to make it earn less where it mattered: no paid loot boxes for minors, no game economy bolted onto studying.

title: A weekly rhythm
description: Five sprints turned a scramble into an engine, with design and content deliberately running a step ahead of development so engineers never wait on a spec. I went from drafting documents in the rhythm to helping run it.

title: Intelligence that matters
description: The same small team pointed its AI at problems bigger than a study app, a model that screens young children for malnutrition risk earlier than the rule-based status quo, and immersive early-learning built for Anganwadi centres in a teacher's own language. Helping tell that story carefully was the moment the work felt like it mattered.

title: The launch that refused to be faked
description: After moving seven times, Project X's launch stopped being a date at all and became a readiness decision. Most launch stories celebrate hitting a deadline. This one is about the quieter discipline of refusing a fake one.

title: A counselling product, against a date that couldn't move
description: NEET results land on a fixed day and every question a student has arrives at once. In under a week we built the whole path: landing page, WhatsApp OTP, lead capture, payment, and a smoke test that refuses to deploy a broken site.

title: Three tiers, and a counsellor with a name
description: NEET Counselling grew a premium tier with a real counsellor behind it, coupon rules scoped per tier, and a webhook that checks whether the OTP actually reached the student instead of assuming it did. Most of what makes money move is plumbing nobody ever sees.

title: Project X gets designed, end to end
description: Every flow the product needs got drawn and argued over: the first run, an ordinary study day, how it works out what you actually know, and the moment it asks for money. After a run of dates that wouldn't hold, there is finally one the product can meet.

title: This site gets torn down and rebuilt
description: The portfolio I narrated in March came apart and went back up: editorial layout, a hero whose last word turns, real product screenshots where gradients used to be. The edit I liked best was a deletion. Three placeholder testimonials came out, because invented praise is still invented.
